title.full: How to spot a scam call

summary.text: Check the caller, the phone number, and the message. Do not give personal or financial information over the phone.

details.heading: Calls from MOH
details.body: MOH is aware of calls falsely informing recipients that the caller is from MOH and requesting personal or financial information over the phone. Do not respond to such calls.

steps.name: Check for a plus sign
steps.text: If a local call has a “+” prefix, do not answer it. This is likely to be a spoofed call.

steps.name: Listen to the message
steps.text: If the caller sends a recorded message, do not treat it as an official call.

steps.name: Protect your information
steps.text: Do not give personal or financial information over the phone, even if the caller says they are from MOH.

steps.name: Verify the caller
steps.text: To check a call from MOH, call MOH General Line 6325 9220. Verify the authenticity of the MOH number and the caller’s full name.

sources.page_title: How to spot a scam call?

quotes.text: Always be sure of the authenticity of instructions before offering any personal or financial information.
Official local calls will usually not have a “+” prefix - this is likely to be a spoofed call which you should not answer.
Official callers will never send you a recorded message.
Official callers will never request your personal or financial information over the phone.
To verify the authenticity of calls from MOH, call MOH General Line 6325 9220 to verify the authenticity of the MOH number and full name of the caller.
MOH is aware of calls falsely informing recipients that the caller is from MOH, requesting your personal or financial information over the phone. We urge recipients not to respond to such calls.
